description: Welcome! Galilean Coders is diving into SPHERE X & PLANET X. We specialize in software engineering, backend systems, and rapid prototyping, driven by a passion for space science. Join us to collaborate on cutting-edge space tech challenges and turn bold ideas into working demos. We are actively seeking teammates skilled in frontend (React), data visualization, or astronomy. Let's reach the stars together!
summary:
SPHEREX Sky Explorer is an interactive astronomical exploration platform developed to compare infrared sky observations captured by NASA's SPHEREX mission at different times.

Our project addresses the challenge of identifying changes in large astronomical datasets by providing a system that processes and compares FITS images. It aligns observations onto a common coordinate grid, generates difference images, and identifies potential regions of change. It also converts candidate pixel positions into celestial coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination).

The platform combines scientific data processing with interactive visualization to make astronomical observations easier to explore and understand. It can help researchers, students, and space enthusiasts investigate unusual changes in the sky and identify interesting regions for further analysis.

Our project supports the exploration of the Planet X hypothesis by providing a practical approach to examining possible astronomical changes. However, the identified candidates are preliminary and do not represent a confirmed discovery of Planet X.
details:
What Does Our Project Do and How Does It Work?

SPHEREX Sky Explorer is designed to compare astronomical observations captured at different times. It uses FITS images from the SPHEREX mission. Our Python backend aligns the selected observations using World Coordinate System (WCS) information and generates a difference image by subtracting the earlier observation from the later one. It then identifies potential regions of change and converts their pixel positions into Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec) coordinates.

What Benefits Does It Have?

The platform makes astronomical image comparison easier and helps users visualize differences between observations. It reduces the effort required for manual comparison and provides candidate locations and celestial coordinates for further investigation.

What Is the Intended Impact?

Our goal is to support astronomical exploration by making SPHEREX infrared data easier to analyze and understand. The project can help researchers, students, and space enthusiasts investigate unusual astronomical changes and explore potential moving or changing objects.

What Tools Did We Use?

  • Python for backend development and scientific processing
  • FastAPI for backend API development
  • Flask for web interface routing
  • NumPy for numerical operations and image comparison
  • Astropy for FITS file handling and WCS coordinate alignment
  • Pandas for candidate data management
  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the web interface
  • Three.js for 3D visualization
  • GitHub for project collaboration and code management
  • Railway for backend hosting / deployment
  • Vercel for frontend hosting
  • Gamma for presentation slides

How Is Our Project Creative?

Our project combines astronomical image processing with interactive visualization. Instead of only displaying individual astronomical images, it compares observations from different dates, generates difference images, highlights potential changes, and provides celestial coordinates for selected candidates.

What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

Our team considered scientific accuracy, image alignment, observation dates, data quality, image noise, possible processing artifacts, usability, and visualization. We also considered the importance of avoiding false conclusions, so potential candidates are treated as signals requiring further investigation rather than confirmed discoveries.
